lens: Hyperscaler-grade — corrective-action loop, machine-queryable schema, hash-chain/signature, automation-first generation
answer: PR #17 fails the hyperscaler bar on the central question: review evidence MUST close the loop into a corrective-action queue, and this wave does not. The synthesis events recorded in evidence/audit-chain.jsonl declare fixuptasks_recommended totaling 64 across the 9 PRs (pr-1:9, pr-2:2, pr-3:9, pr-5:10, pr-6:2, pr-7:10, pr-8:6, pr-9:6, pr-11:10), yet registries/cross-cutting/fixuptasks.jsonl contains only 2 F-PR* rows — both pre-existing (M02-P06 scoped, not PR-derived). The naming-justification block in the PR body promises `F-PR<N>-NN` stable IDs but the canonical fixuptask registry has no such rows landed. That is theater: a Stripe/Palantir review pipeline would refuse the merge because the audit-chain claims 64 open blockers that are not actionable downstream. Second, the artifact schema is machine-parseable JSON but is NOT hash-chained (no `prev_hash`/`content_hash`), NOT signed (no `signed_by`/`signature`), and reviewer_id format `codex-F<facet>-pr-<N>-r<round>[-rebuttal]` is doctrine-conforming as `<tool>-<facet_id>-<change_id>-<round_qualifier>` but lacks a content digest binding evidence to merge SHA. The audit-chain row does carry `merge_commit_sha` in r2 artifacts (cdc53bf...) which is the only verifiable anchor. Third, per [[feedback_automate_everything]] this wave is hand-emitted with extreme template repetition — 18 facet × 9 PRs = 162 r1+r2 files where r2 bodies are near-identical boilerplate ("Round-2 F1 reconciliation preserved consensus finding"). At 9 PRs × 18 artifacts = 162 evidence files + 9 synthesis = 171 artifacts (PR meta says 74+9=83 but diff totals 173 changed files), the wave is large but trivially generable from a single template + per-PR finding tuples. This should be a `omc msr backfill --prs 1,2,3,5,6,7,8,9,11` codex command writing all 162 files deterministically. Manual emission is non-scalable: the next 20-PR catch-up will demand 360+ artifacts. Verdict: changes_requested — not because the recorded findings are wrong, but because the loop is open (fixuptasks not registered) and the generator is not codified.

findings.summary: Audit-chain claims 64 fixuptasks_recommended across 9 PRs but registries/cross-cutting/fixuptasks.jsonl has zero F-PR<N>-NN rows — the corrective-action loop never closes; downstream PRs cannot dequeue from a queue that does not exist
findings.recommended_action: Block: emit all 64 F-PR<N>-NN rows into registries/cross-cutting/fixuptasks.jsonl with severity, facet_origin, change_id, summary, section_anchor before merge OR in an immediate follow-up PR referenced by the audit-chain row. Without this, future PRs cannot satisfy the FixupTask gate against this wave.

findings.summary: Evidence generation is hand-emitted at 162+ artifacts with near-identical r2 rebuttal bodies — violates [[feedback_automate_everything]]; next 20-PR catch-up will demand 360+ artifacts
findings.recommended_action: Land a `omc msr backfill` (or `cargo run -p oya-dev-cli -- msr backfill --prs <list>`) command that takes a per-PR finding tuple file and deterministically emits all r1+r2+synthesis artifacts. Codify the template once.

findings.summary: Evidence artifacts lack hash-chain (no prev_hash/content_hash) and signature (no signed_by/signature) — Stripe/Palantir review pipelines require both to detect post-merge mutation and bind evidence to reviewer identity
findings.recommended_action: Extend the evidence schema with `content_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON sans hash field), `prev_hash` (previous artifact in PR's facet chain), and `signed_by` (key fingerprint). Audit-chain rows should reference content_hash of synthesis. Enforce in oya-foundry-audit-chain-domain.

findings.recommended_action: Either confirm those 5 comments are wave-scope (and rename field `wave_review_comments_addressed`) or replace with per-PR comment ID lists. Add lint to oya-foundry-audit-chain validating that per-change_id payloads cite at least one change_id-specific comment.

consensus_addendum.antithesis_steelman: Retroactive review evidence is intrinsically lower-value than pre-merge review; demanding hash-chain + signature + automation for a documentation-grade wave is gold-plating that delays the corrective loop further. The PR's existence at all is net-positive vs. the prior state of zero evidence for those 9 merged PRs; perfect should not be enemy of good. Counter-counter: the PR explicitly claims fixuptasks_recommended:64 in machine-readable audit-chain rows — that claim creates compliance debt regardless of retroactive scope, and a downstream gate reading audit-chain will believe the count.
consensus_addendum.tradeoff_tension: Speed-to-evidence (land 171 artifacts now, even hand-emitted) vs. loop-closure-correctness (refuse merge until FixupTask registry matches audit-chain claims). Picking speed leaves a 64-task phantom queue; picking correctness blocks the wave until a generator + registry-write is built, which is itself a multi-day slice.
consensus_addendum.synthesis_if_viable: Merge PR #17 as-is for the evidence artifacts, but immediately follow with a small surgical PR that (a) emits the 64 F-PR<N>-NN rows into the canonical FixupTask registry from the existing synthesis JSONs (deterministic transform, <50 LoC), and (b) lands the `msr backfill` generator. Audit-chain rows then become truthful retroactively.
